Once [Riaz ON](riaz-on-quick-start.html) runs, replace its table with your own.
Supply the complete DE result, not only significant genes.

## Prepare the input

For a DESeq2 table, use these columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `symbol` | Gene symbol matching the gene-set resource. |
| `log2FoldChange` | Signed effect for your comparison. |
| `stat` | Signed ranking statistic, normally the Wald statistic. |
| `pvalue` | Gene-level raw P value. |
| `padj` | Gene-level adjusted P value. |

Check which group is in the numerator before writing the direction sentence.
A DESeq2 likelihood-ratio statistic is unsigned; the
[extended R guide](getting-started.html) explains that case and edgeR/limma
inputs.

## Run one analysis

This example assumes a human DESeq2 Wald-test result and the resource prepared
during Riaz ON. Change the two paths and the direction sentence.

```{r own-de, eval=FALSE}
library(lisaR)

result <- run_lisa(
  de = "de_treated_vs_control.tsv",
  output_dir = "lisa-treated-vs-control",
  species = "Homo sapiens",
  method = "DESeq2",
  positive_direction = "Higher in treated than in control"
)

stopifnot(identical(result$gate, "PASS"))
browseURL(result$report_index)
```

Choose a new output directory. STANDARD is the default; it includes PNG and
SVG figures, source tables and figure recipes. Add `pdf = TRUE` if needed.

lisaR uses the supplied DE results. It does not re-estimate your effects or fit
your experimental design. For another species, prepare the corresponding
[membership resource](resources-and-provenance.html); do not substitute the
human resource.

**Next: [Read your report](read-your-report.html).**
